chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Sindi ibn al-Rabi', from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abu Jamilyah, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked: What do you say about a person in ihram who breaks one horn of a gazelle while in the hal (non-sanctuary)? He said: 'Upon him is one-quarter of the value of the gazelle.' I asked: And if he breaks both its horns? He said: 'Upon him is half its value, which he gives in charity.' I asked: And if he puts out its two eyes? He said: 'Upon him is its full value.' I asked: And if he breaks one of its two arms? He said: 'Upon him is half its value.' I asked: And if he breaks one of its two legs? He said: 'Upon him is half its value.' I asked: And if he kills it? He said: 'Upon him is its full value.' He said: I asked: And if he does this to it while it is in ihram in the hal? He said: 'Upon him is the blood (dam) he must pour out, and upon him is this value, if he is in ihram in the haram (sanctuary).'

key_terms.الْحَرَمُ: The sanctuary or holy area (e.g., Mecca)
key_terms.الْحِلُّ: The non-sanctuary area outside the holy boundaries
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A pilgrim in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for breaking a gazelle's horn while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes a graded scale of *diyah* (compensation) for a pilgrim in *ihram* who injures a gazelle in the *hal* (non-sanctuary), ranging from a quarter to the full value depending on the specific injury. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between minor injuries in the *hal* and the more severe penalty of shedding blood (*dam*) plus full compensation when the injury occurs within the *haram*. This detailed classification underscores the precision of Imami fiqh in balancing ritual sanctity with practical legal rulings for pilgrims.
